abstract.p: Previous work (i.e., SPIDER [51]) has considered a patch as "safe" if it only restricts a function's accepted input space without affecting its behavior for valid inputs, and it has formally defined source-code-level properties that need to hold for a patch to be considered as functionality-preserving. Our goal is to aid the patch verification process by identifying, highlighting, and verifying patch-introduced changes directly in binaries. We aim to verify analogous properties, which we call Safe to Apply (StA) properties, without the need for source code, by directly comparing a patched binary with its original version.
